1.why: Pressure is force divided by area, so smaller area gives higher pressure.

wrong.d: Force alone does not determine pressure.

2.why: P stands for pressure, measured in pascals.

3.why: Wind blows from high pressure to low pressure areas.

wrong.a: Wind does not blow from low to high.
wrong.d: Humidity does not drive wind directly.

cover.title: How air pressure creates wind
cover.subtitle: Invisible air particles push on everything around us. Discover how differences in air pressure make the wind blow across regions.
cover.subject: Physics · Pressure
cover.fun_fact: Air pushes on your body with a weight equal to a car, but internal pressure balances it out.
story.title: The invisible pushing air
story.lead: Meteorologists report changing weather patterns across Indonesia as air pressure shifts [1]. Air is made of tiny particles that move fast and push on all surfaces [2].
stat.1.label: newtons force on 5 m² area producing 6 pascal pressure
stat.2.label: pascal pressure when area is 1 m² with 30 N force
stat.3.label: square meters area when force is 30 N
story.body_1: Air surrounds our planet in a deep layer called the atmosphere. Even though we cannot see air, its particles have mass and weight. They collide with everything around them, creating atmospheric pressure [2].
story.body_2: When the Sun heats the Earth unevenly, warm air rises and creates low-pressure zones. Cooler air rushes in from high-pressure zones, creating wind [3]. Understanding air pressure helps scientists forecast storms and weather changes [1].
timeline.1.text: Sun begins heating the land, and air pressure is stable.
timeline.2.text: Warm air rises, forming a low-pressure zone and strong winds.
timeline.3.text: Cooler air settles, balancing regional air pressure.
physics.title: Force, area and pressure
physics.body_1: Pressure tells us how much force is spread over a specific surface area. If a force is concentrated on a small area, the pressure is very high.
physics.body_2: We calculate pressure by dividing the push force by the surface area. A smaller area gives a higher pressure for the same force.
physics.assumptions: We assume the force acts uniformly and perpendicularly across the flat surface area.
table.note: Same force on a smaller area creates higher pressure.

lab.title: Bottle pressure lab
lab.step_1: Get a plastic bottle and poke a small hole near the bottom with a pin.
lab.step_2: Cover hole with your finger, fill the bottle with water, and screw cap on.
lab.step_3: Remove your finger and observe how air pressure and water interact.
lab.question: Why does water stop flowing when the cap is tightly closed?
